% note: $d$ is the vote of $k$ Haiku-max samples minus one Opus-medium answer, in points, paired over the same puzzles; a positive $d$ means the vote scored higher.
% note: The Test~B2 row is the pre-registered test at B2's own $k$~=~6 (Study~1b's rule for a cost-matched vote). Its pooled $d$ and interval are Test~B2's stamped confirmatory values, unchanged: $p$~\ensuremath{\leq}~0.00011, below its Holm threshold of 0.00833; reading: shown no worse by \ensuremath{>}~margin (Holm-adjusted), in all three views. Its accuracy, format compliance and costs are pre-specified descriptive, not part of the test. One comparison, one interval: free analysis 3's own interval for this vote is not printed.
% note: Error-rate ratio $R$: the vote's errors over Opus-medium's on the same puzzles. Near the ceiling it sits beside $d$; on the Test~B2 row it is Study~1b's stamped value for Test~B2, pre-specified descriptive, reported beside the test and not part of it. The post hoc rows have none: free analysis 3 stamps no error-rate ratio.
% note: The other vote rows are post hoc descriptive sensitivity: Study~1b's spec set no sensitivity analysis over $k$, so their $d$ and cost ratio carry no $p$-value, no Holm correction and no reading against the margin, and they leave B2 unchanged. Their accuracy, format compliance and cost are Study~1b's pre-specified vote curve.
% note: One Haiku-max sample ($k$~=~1) is Test~B1's challenger and is reported with the Study~1b tests.
% note: Cost: US dollars per answer at list price (item~9b); a vote of $k$ samples costs $k$ times one sample's list cost per answer. Every value in the spend share or cost ratio column is the vote's pooled list cost per answer over Opus-medium's: a cost ratio on the post hoc rows and, on the Test~B2 row, B2's spend share, as ⟦TAB-01⟧ prints it. The samples per comparator answer that set a cost-matched $k$ (Opus-medium's cost per answer over one Haiku-max sample's, as in Panel~1) are printed to two decimals; a vote's cost over Opus-medium's, as reported for Test~B2 with the Study~1b tests, to three.
% note: Format compliance: the Haiku-max samples the votes are taken over, and Opus-medium's answers on its row.
% note: Panel~1: per-shape intervals are printed only here (one comparison, one interval): free analysis 3 also stamps per-shape intervals at each $k$, drawn with other seeds, and they are not printed.
% note: \ensuremath{\leq}~marks a $p$ at the smallest value the bootstrap can return (no resample reached the margin).
